findings.motion: H.R. 1, For the People Act, On Passage (Roll Call 118)
findings.note: Voted yes on passage of H.R. 1 as a member of the House. Section 1903 of the bill (text at https://www.congress.gov/116/bills/hr1/BILLS-116hr1eh.htm) says that where a state requires ID to vote, the state must let a voter in person or by mail meet it with a sworn written statement signed under penalty of perjury attesting to identity and eligibility. First-time voters who registered by mail are excepted.
subjects: sworn statement in place of ID

findings.motion: Passage of H.R. 1, For the People Act (Roll Call 118)
findings.note: McAdams voted yea on passage of H.R. 1, a broad elections bill; the bill passed 234 to 193. The page does not itself describe the bill's ID provisions.

findings.passage: “Utahns believe in fair play,” he said. “You don’t rig the system to protect your own power. You don’t move the lines, especially after voters have already engaged in the current election. Fair elections mean stable rules, transparency, and respect for voters.”
findings.note: Campaign press release quoting him on fair elections, in a dispute over congressional district lines. It does not mention ID or citizenship proof.

findings.passage: “When politicians try to change the rules or rig elections, it’s not them who pay the price – it’s us, the voters. They stay in power, and we lose our voice.”
findings.note: His quoted words in an endorsement release. The endorser's own words say he will support the Freedom to Vote Act and the John R. Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act; those are the endorser's words, not his.
